children.text: Lake Buhi is a freshwater lake of about 1,700–1,800 hectares in Buhi, Camarines Sur, set in the valley between Mount Iriga (Mount Asog) and Mount Malinao. It is home to the sinarapan, known as the world's smallest commercially harvested fish, and you can cross it by boat to Itbog Falls.
Lake Buhi is a freshwater lake in the municipality of Buhi on the Bicol peninsula, Camarines Sur. Wikipedia gives its area as about 17–18 km², with an average depth of about
8m
and a maximum depth of about

, while the Buhi municipal government says about 1,800 hectares. The lake lies in the valley between Mount Iriga (Mount Asog) and Mount Malinao, and the slopes of Mount Iriga come down to one side of it. Buhi town is described as about
75km
northeast of Legazpi and about
53km
from Naga City.

There are two stories about how the lake formed. The most common account is that a 1641 earthquake triggered a landslide from Mount Iriga (Asog) that dammed nearby streams. The other theory is that an eruption of the now-dormant Mount Iriga created the lake. The rivers that flow into the lake are the Buhi and Iriga rivers, and the water leaves through the Tabao River. The lake has also long been a livelihood for local people. The Buhi municipal government says it was named the cleanest lake in the Philippines in 1996 under the National Clean and Green Program.

What made the lake famous is the sinarapan (Mistichthys luzonensis). It is known as the world's smallest commercially harvested fish and is said to be endemic to lakes in the Rinconada area. However, overfishing and environmental change have reduced it, and one guide says it is on the brink of extinction. So rather than expecting to taste sinarapan at the lake, it is better to visit in the spirit of understanding the conservation efforts and the local way of life. The lake also reportedly has native fish such as irin-irin, dalag, puyo, kotnag and native catfish, and introduced species such as Nile tilapia and carp.

For travelers, the appeal of Buhi is less the lake itself than the trip across it. You cross by boat to the Itbog twin falls, enjoy the scenery made by Mount Asog behind the lake, and reviewers say that on early mornings without cloud Mayon Volcano can be seen in the distance. The town is not large, so facilities are limited; plan your schedule and transport in advance. In the 2020 census Buhi had about 81,000 residents in 38 barangays. Mount Malinao, at 1,548 m, rises to the east of the lake and Mount Iriga (Asog), at 1,196 m, to the west, and this view of two mountains on either side of the lake is characteristic of the area.
This is the habitat of the sinarapan, known as the world's smallest commercially harvested fish. Lakes Manapao and Katugday, about
3km
west of Buhi, are small mountain lakes where a project to repopulate sinarapan is under way.

The slopes of Mount Iriga (Asog) rise behind the lake. Hiking guides describe knife-edged slopes running toward the lake. The view of the lake from the mountain is also famous.
Buhi is said to have Pongol Hot Spring, Balerite Resort, Lologon Resort and Sinagpan Spring Resort. Combining the lake with a hot spring makes a good half-day trip.
The Saint Francis of Assisi Parish Church, completed in 1884, and the Buhi History Monument are in town. You can stop by briefly on the way to the lake.

blocks.title: The forest and birds around the lake

children.text: The forest around the lake is said to hold at least 25 bird species, five of them endemic. Birds such as the Philippine pygmy woodpecker and the Philippine hanging parrot are mentioned. Long-tailed macaques and flying lizards are also said to live there.

The lake supplies a National Power Corporation hydroelectric plant built in 1952 that averages about 2.8 megawatts, and it is used to irrigate rice fields in the Rinconada area and Iriga City. The Buhi municipal government says it irrigates about 13,000 hectares of rice land.

Buhi has a warm, humid climate. The warmest months are March to June (average about
), the rainy season runs from August to February, and annual rainfall is about 2,750 mm. October is said to be the wettest month.

The December–May dry season is best. One guide says October to January brings heavy rain and a higher typhoon risk, so in the wet season keep your schedule loose and check whether boats are running. Reviewers say Mayon Volcano can be seen across the lake on early mornings with few clouds.

Lodging in Buhi town is limited. A 2019 review says the only hotel near the town center was Villa Florencia, where a family room with air conditioning and a hot shower cost about $40. That review found no Wi-Fi, so check whether this has changed. Another review stayed at Lake Buhi Resort near the lake, so you can also arrange a boat through the resort. If lodging is short, it is safer to stay in Naga City or Iriga City and take a van in the morning.

Food centers on freshwater fish dishes such as tilapia caught in the lake, and Bicolano cooking. A review says there were no chain restaurants, but there was a bar near the church (Dwinox Bar) and a small supermarket. At the local market you can buy fresh fish, vegetables and snacks. Sinarapan is endangered, so it is better to support conservation than to eat it. Restaurants are few, so bring water and snacks when you go to the falls.

Before it is a tourist site, the lake is a source of livelihood for the area. Tilapia farming and fishing, rice irrigation and hydroelectric power all depend on the one lake. On September 22, 2007, a mass fish kill threatened fishers' livelihoods; the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources blamed sulfur dioxide from the Iriga side, but the volcanology institute did not accept that conclusion. Knowing these stories changes how you see the lake. If you meet fishing boats on the lake, do not touch the fishers' gear, and ask permission before taking photos.
Leave early from Naga or Iriga. Crossing the lake and trekking to the falls takes at least half a day.
Bring a waterproof bag. Spray from the boat or rain can wet your things.
Bring insect repellent, sunscreen, water, snacks, comfortable sandals or shoes and a towel.
Agree on the boat fare and the return time before you set out. Service varies with the weather.
Check whether life jackets are provided, and always wear one.
Flight routes to Naga can change, so check the latest information.
Mayon is sometimes visible across the lake in the morning, so get out early.
In the rainy season boats and the falls path can be slippery, so check the weather and whether boats are running. Sinarapan needs conservation, so avoid catching or eating it.
In 2007 there was a mass fish kill in the lake, and views differed on the cause. Check local notices on water quality.
Boat fares and safety gear differ by operator, so check in advance.
When riding a motorbike on rural roads, wear a helmet and be careful.
Lodging and restaurants are limited, so make a lodging plan before you travel.
Many reviews are old, so check the latest announcements for rates and schedules.
Mount Iriga, west of the lake, is a hiking destination with a horseshoe-shaped crater and lake views.
